name: ONNX Runtime GenAI
notable_features: Implements the generative loop on top of ONNX Runtime: pre/post-processing, the ORT inference call, logits processing, search and sampling, KV cache management, and grammar specification for tool calling.
The broadest EPU coverage of any engine here: CPU, CUDA, DirectML, OpenVINO, QNN (Qualcomm NPU), WebGPU, AMD GPU, and TensorRT-RTX.

Official architectures include Granite, Granite MoE Hybrid, Phi, and gpt-oss — Microsoft-adjacent models — plus Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, Nemotron, InternLM2, SmolLM3, ERNIE 4.5, ChatGLM, Whisper and LFM2 (language + vision + speech).
Builds for x86, x64 and arm64 on Linux, Windows, Mac and Android; Objective-C bindings exist, iOS requires building from source.
Powers Foundry Local, Windows ML and the Visual Studio Code AI Toolkit — real shipping products, not experiments.
Multi-LoRA and speculative decoding listed as features.

Grammar-based tool calling built into the generative loop itself (grammar specification alongside pre/post-processing, logits processing, search and sampling and KV cache management) rather than delegated to an external constraint library
hardware_caveats: Quantization coverage is limited and comes from the ONNX quantization toolchain, not from the engine: the documented CPU example is a pre-exported int4 block-quantized ONNX tree (e.g. cpu-int4-rtn-block-32-acc-level-4). You must pick a quantization variant that already exists on the Hub or produce one with Optimum; the engine does not invent quant schemes.
Because quantization is baked into the exported ONNX graph, switching precision means re-exporting the model, not flipping a runtime flag — a real operational difference from GGUF/EXL2 workflows.
The iOS binding requires a source build (marked with ^ in the README's API table).
Main-branch examples track main and can be ahead of the latest stable release; the README tells you to check out the matching version tag (e.g. v0.11.5) for examples matching a stable install.
Architecture support is a maintained list, not a blanket promise — stable diffusion and multi-modal models are still under development or on the roadmap at access time.
best_for: ONNX-first teams and Windows/Foundry Local users who want a supported, vendor-backed path rather than a hobby project.
NPUs and other accelerators that only ONNX Runtime targets: QNN for Qualcomm, DirectML for broad Windows GPU support, WebGPU for browsers.
Arm64 and Android devices, where GGUF tooling is thin and an ONNX export with an int4 variant is often the only viable path.
Offline/on-device features embedded in a larger ONNX-based product — one runtime, one dependency graph.
Specifying model architecture coverage deliberately: Granite, Phi and gpt-oss are first-class.
avoid_for: Maximum tok/s on a CUDA or AMD GPU — GPU-first engines exist for that.
Workloads needing GGUF/EXL2/GPTQ quantization flexibility; the format choice is made at export time and is narrow.
Multi-user serving — no scheduler beyond the batch/batch_size search options.
Any architecture not in the supported list; the list moves and needs re-checking per release.
notes: Backend names in supported_backends follow the README's own 'Hardware Acceleration' row (CPU, CUDA, DirectML, NvTensorRtRtx, OpenVINO, QNN, WebGPU, AMD GPU) normalized to the repo's vocabulary where they map cleanly; directml, qnn, webgpu, amd-gpu and tensorrt-rtx are extensions of the schema's example enum, which describes rather than enumerates it. Qualcomm NPU is recorded as qnn rather than npu because QNN is Qualcomm-specific and NPU alone would imply vendor neutrality. 'Limited quantization coverage' is a characterization of the workflow, not a quoted claim — the README does not say the words. ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-04 (0 months), latest release v0.17.0 published 2026-09-28, 152 contributors, open_issues_count 251 (issues PLUS pull requests), NOT archived, 1132 stars. DEPLOYMENT: NO EVIDENCE OF PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT FOUND as of 2026-10-04 - see [[ev-production-evidence-is-scarce-and-nearly-always-single-site]]. FEATURE AXES - STRUCTURED OUTPUT is the axis this engine gains most and it is qualitatively different from the others: 'grammar specification for tool calling' is an in-engine first-class component of the generative loop rather than something supplied by a companion library, which is unusual at this EPU breadth and is the honest answer to 'can this do constrained generation on a phone NPU'. MULTIMODAL is stated per-architecture rather than as a blanket claim, which is the more honest form and worth preserving: LFM2 'language + vision + speech input', Phi 'language + vision', Qwen 'language + vision', plus Whisper and a separate stable-diffusion path. The supported-architecture list is broader than this record previously implied and includes DeepSeek, Nemotron, gpt-oss, Granite MoE Hybrid and Fara. PREFIX CACHING, CHUNKED PREFILL, SPECULATIVE DECODING and DISAGGREGATED P/D: none appear in the README, so all four are UNSTATED; the record's existing 'scheduling: none' stands, qualified by the fact that KV cache MANAGEMENT is present even though scheduling is not.
